pages.title: The First Rule Is Distance
pages.text: $(bold)Warning:$() Choose a place whose loss is survivable. A failed Draconic Reactor can erase a vast area, so keep it far from bases, chunk borders, irreplaceable terrain, and other reactors. Keep the whole site loaded and give containment its own redundant power.

pages.title: Six Clear Lines from the Core
pages.text: The measured rule is simple: the Core scans six cardinal directions. A component must face it across clear air at a distance of 4–7 blocks; the first solid thing on that line must be the intended component.$(br2)This example puts four stabilizers in a horizontal plane, leaving the vertical axis for one or two Energy Injectors.

pages.name: Four Stabilizers
pages.text: Top-view sketch at minimum distance. Purple only marks the real Reactor Core—do not place glass. Four stabilizers stand four blocks away and face inward.

pages.name: Vertical Injector Axis
pages.text: For the horizontal stabilizer layout above, place an Energy Injector 4–7 blocks directly above the Core and face it downward. Feed containment power into its outer side; a second injector may be placed below. The entire arrangement may be rotated together.

pages.title: Core and Stabilizers
pages.text: The Reactor Core and its Stabilizers are late Fusion products. Build all five before choosing the site; exactly four stabilizers are required for one reactor.

pages.title: Energy Injector
pages.text: The Energy Injector is also made by Fusion. One is sufficient; a second may stand opposite it. Keep any spare away from the reactor site rather than storing every critical part beside the hazard.
